subject: Unexplained regional ingest spike and EU/US token attribution on May 7 invoice
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmeinc.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+billing@acmeinc.com
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible double-counting on May 2026 invoice (hourly spike May 7)

Hi Kimberly,

We just received our May invoice (invoice_202605.pdf attached) and noticed a large hour-long spike on May 7 ~02:00 UTC that pushed us into an overage tier. Our finance team flagged that most of the tokens in that window are attributed to EU region and are being charged with VAT, but our traffic shows the requests originated from a US-based ingestion pipeline. Can you please help
- Explain the attribution logic that assigned these tokens to EU
- Provide raw usage export for the hour (per-req ID / timestamp / region tag)
- Confirm whether retries or CDN duplication could have caused duplicate token counts

We need this evidence to file a VAT reallocation with our tax team and to request a pro-rata credit if there was incorrect regional attribution. Can you escalate?

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Cloudware
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible double-counting on May 2026 invoice (hourly spike May 7)

Hi Carlos — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the surprise. I’m looping in Ben (metering) and Marissa (billing/credits) to pull the export and do an initial attribution check.

Ben — can you pull the per-request usage export for 2026-05-07 01:30–03:30 UTC and confirm:
- raw request ids, request timestamps, routed region, token counts, and any retry flags
- whether our regional routing or fallback rules could attribute US-origin traffic to EU (there was a brief EU region outage last week)

Marissa — if it looks like misattribution or duplication, can you flag for a pro-rata credit and VAT reallocation? I’ll need a short summary we can share with Acme and with our finance team.

Carlos — attaching a HubSpot ticket link so we maintain a single thread of record. I’ll follow up by EOD Monday.

—Kimberly
Director, Customer Billing
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 07:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible double-counting on May 2026 invoice (hourly spike May 7)

Hi all — I pulled the raw logs and ran a quick dedupe + attribution pass. Summary first, details below and I attached usage_export_202605.zip (CSV with per-request rows).

Summary:
- There were ~78k extra token-attribution events between 2026-05-07 02:05–02:55 UTC that appear to be duplicates of legitimate US-origin requests.
- Cause: we saw a cluster of retries from a third-party CDN in front of Acme’s ingestion endpoint. The CDN retried with slightly different edge IPs; our routing layer (geo by edge IP) attributed some of those retries to EU edges.
- Net effect: ~64k tokens were billed under EU region (VAT) instead of being billed under US region (no VAT).
- Proposed remediation: 1) issue a pro-rata credit for tokens double-counted (approx 78k tokens), 2) reclassify the affected token rows to US for VAT purposes, 3) share the raw CSV export so Acme can reconcile.

Detailed notes and evidence:
- Attached CSV columns: request_id, ts_utc, client_ip, routed_region, token_count, retry_flag
- Example duplicate: request_id root-req-9a1f, ts_utc 2026-05-07T02:12:18Z, token_count 842 — appears twice with different client_ip & routed_region values (us-east / eu-central).
- Our routing service logs show a transient EU edge failover window between 02:03–02:08 UTC for a subset of traffic; however retries continued through 02:55 due to CDN backoff behavior.

Next steps I’m taking:
- Mark the affected rows in a CSV (col flagged) and upload to the HubSpot ticket.
- Recommend a one-off credit: calculation attached in the CSV footer (78,210 tokens * per-token rate).

Marissa — please confirm the exact credit amount and VAT handling. Carlos — let me know if you want us to redact any IPs before sending the CSV to your tax team.

—Ben
Senior Billing Analyst, Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acmeinc.com>

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:11:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Possible double-counting on May 2026 invoice (hourly spike May 7)

Thanks Ben — that aligns with what our logs show (CDN retries behaved oddly during that maintenance window). We do need the CSV with the flagged rows and the proposed credit calculation so we can:
1) submit a VAT reallocation request to our tax advisors (they want proof of region-by-request),
2) accept the pro-rata credit to clear the invoice dispute.

Invoice reference: ACME-INV-202605-093
Please include the VAT adjustment line item (so our AP team can process the corrected invoice). We prefer minimal PII in the file; redacted IPs are fine.

Appreciate the quick look — once we have the credit note and VAT reallocation we’ll close the dispute.

Regards,
Carlos
